passage: I'm Mridul's older cousin, staying with them for the holidays. Last year he and Siddharth just played cricket and fought over whose turn it was. Now it's different. They sit on the water tank whispering, and they stop when I come up. Yesterday some boys asked Mridul why Siddharth didn't come for swimming. "He just didn't," Mridul said, and changed the subject. Later I heard Siddharth tell him, "Thanks for not telling." I don't know the secret. But Mridul walked him all the way home, which he never used to do.

qa.q: Where do Mridul and Siddharth sit to whisper?
qa.a: They sit on the water tank.

qa.q: Why might Mridul have changed the subject when the boys asked about swimming?
qa.a: He seemed protective of Siddharth and loyal to him, wanting to keep his secret.

qa.q: What would you advise the cousin about the secret?
qa.a: Respect their privacy, and step in only if something seems unsafe, since trust between friends matters a lot at this age.

qa.q: How does Siddharth seem to see Mridul now?
qa.a: As someone he can trust, which is why he quietly thanks him for not telling.

grounding: It shows, from a cousin's view, two boys moving from playmates to loyal friends who keep each other's secrets.

passage:
June: Usha and Eshaan only met at the park swings. They talked about nothing except who could go higher.
August: At a family sleepover at Usha's, the lights went off. Eshaan went very quiet, then whispered, "I'm scared of the dark. Don't tell anyone." Usha found the torch and said, "I'm scared of dogs." They made a pinky promise.
October: At school a boy teased, "Eshaan sleeps with a night-light, I bet!" Usha looked straight at him. "So what? Everyone's scared of something." Later she whispered to Eshaan, "I didn't tell. I never will."

qa.q: What secret did Usha share in return?
qa.a: She said she's scared of dogs.

qa.q: Why did Usha share her own fear after Eshaan's?
qa.a: She wanted him to feel safe and not alone, so she traded a secret and made them equal.

qa.q: How did Usha handle the teasing, and what else could she do if it continued?
qa.a: She calmly backed Eshaan without revealing anything; if it kept happening, they could tell a teacher together.

qa.q: What is it like for Eshaan when Usha says "I never will"?
qa.a: He likely feels relieved and trusted, knowing his secret is safe with a real friend. 🤍

grounding: It shows a friendship growing over months from swing-mates to friends who share and guard secrets.

passage: Aadhya, you asked who my best friend was. At ten, it was Gopal. Before that, boys were just people to play gulli-danda with. Then one monsoon we found a puppy under the school bridge. My father didn't allow dogs, so we kept it in Gopal's cowshed. It was our secret for three months. We took turns saving chapatis for it. One day Gopal's elder brother found out and asked, "Hemant, whose puppy is this?" I said it was mine, so Gopal wouldn't be scolded alone. We both got scolded. But after that, we told each other everything.

qa.q: Where did the two friends keep the puppy?
qa.a: In Gopal's cowshed.

qa.q: Why did young Hemant claim the puppy?
qa.a: Hemant wanted to protect Gopal from being scolded alone, showing loyalty to a friend.

qa.q: What could the boys have done differently about the puppy?
qa.a: They might have asked a trusted adult to help find it a home, so they didn't have to keep a secret from their families.

qa.q: How might Gopal have felt when Hemant claimed the puppy?
qa.a: Grateful and closer to Hemant, which may be why they told each other everything afterwards.

grounding: It shows, told by an elder, a friendship deepening through a shared secret and an act of loyalty.

passage: Floodwater had crept into the lane, and Bhupen's family was moving to the relief camp at the school. As they packed, his friend Ujjwal came wading over. 'Remember our secret tin?' Ujjwal whispered. They had buried it under the jackfruit tree last year: marbles, a note about how Ujjwal still cried when thunder came, and Bhupen's confession that he'd broken his father's radio. 'The water might get it,' Bhupen said. They dug it up together, wet to the knees. 'Keep it safe,' Ujjwal said. 'You're the only one I told.' Bhupen tucked the tin under his shirt.

qa.q: Where had the friends buried their secret tin?
qa.a: Under the jackfruit tree.

qa.q: Why did Ujjwal say 'You're the only one I told'?
qa.a: Ujjwal wanted Bhupen to know how deep the trust was and how much their friendship mattered.

qa.q: What does keeping each other's secrets do for a friendship like this?
qa.a: It builds deep trust and loyalty, turning simple playmates into close friends who can share fears.

qa.q: What would change if Bhupen had told others about Ujjwal and thunder?
qa.a: Ujjwal would likely feel betrayed, and their friendship could lose the trust that holds it together.

grounding: Illustrates a friendship deepening through loyalty and shared secrets despite the stress of a flood.

passage: On the colony terrace in Delhi, Harish sat hugging his knees. 'Everyone's going to the swimming pool on Sunday,' he said. 'I can't swim. Don't tell.' Lalremsiami nodded. 'I won't.' On Sunday, the others teased, 'Harish is scared of water!' Lalremsiami said nothing about the secret. She just said, 'He's coming with me to the library instead.' Harish looked at her and grinned. Later he gave her a sticker of a whale. 'Because you're my real friend,' he said.

qa.q: What did Harish give Lalremsiami later?
qa.a: He gave her a sticker of a whale.

qa.q: Why did Harish grin at Lalremsiami?
qa.a: He felt relieved and grateful that she kept his secret and covered for him.

qa.q: What was wise about how Lalremsiami handled the teasing?
qa.a: She did not reveal his secret and gave him a way out with dignity, showing loyalty.

qa.q: How might the teasing children see Harish and Lalremsiami's friendship?
qa.a: They might notice the two are close and that she stands up for him, even if they don't know why.

grounding: Shows a friendship moving to loyalty through a shared secret that one friend protects.

passage:
"Tushar, can I tell you something? Don't tell anyone."
"Okay." Tushar put down his cricket ball.
Sonali, ten, looked at her shoes. "I can't swim. Everyone thinks I can. And the school trip has a pool day."
"That's the secret?"
"Don't laugh."
"I'm not laughing. I couldn't swim till last year."
"Really?"
"Really. My cousin taught me in the river."
"Will you tell the others?"
"No. Friends don't do that." He thought. "On pool day, I'll stay in the shallow end with you. We'll say we're racing."
Sonali smiled for the first time that afternoon.

qa.q: What did Sonali say the school trip had?
qa.a: A pool day.

qa.q: Why did Sonali look at her shoes before telling Tushar?
qa.a: She felt embarrassed and nervous about sharing a secret she had kept from everyone.

qa.q: What did Tushar do that made him a good friend here?
qa.a: He listened without laughing, shared his own story and offered a plan that kept her secret.

qa.q: How does Tushar see keeping Sonali's secret?
qa.a: He sees it as simply what friends do, part of being loyal.

grounding: Shows a friendship deepening from play to loyalty when one child shares a secret and the other keeps it.

passage: I'm Rukmini. Shankar and I used to just cycle round the colony together after school, racing to the water tank. We didn't talk much. Last winter, sitting on the tank wall, I told him something I'd never told anyone: I don't want to be a doctor like everyone in my family expects. I want to play drums. He didn't laugh. He said, "You tap on everything anyway." The next week he brought me two old chopsticks as drumsticks. He's never told a soul. Now I tell him everything first, before anyone else.

qa.q: Where did Rukmini and Shankar sit when she told him?
qa.a: On the water tank wall.

qa.q: How did Rukmini feel after Shankar kept the secret?
qa.a: Rukmini felt trusted and close to him, relieved to have someone who understood.

qa.q: What would you advise Rukmini to do with her drum dream?
qa.a: Keep practising and find a calm moment to talk to a family member Rukmini trusts about it.

qa.q: What might Shankar have been thinking when he brought the chopsticks?
qa.a: He probably wanted to show he took the dream seriously and was on Rukmini's side.

grounding: Shows a child's friendship moving from cycling together to loyalty built on a shared secret.

passage:
Class teacher's note, Hansa, Thursday
I've noticed Akash (11) and Kunal have grown much closer this term. Earlier they only played football together. Today some boys teased Kunal about his speech practice, asking what he does in the counsellor's room. Akash knew, because Kunal had told him, but he said only, "It's his business," and walked Kunal to class. Kunal looked relieved. I thanked Akash privately and spoke to the boys who teased. I'll keep an eye on how Kunal is doing.

qa.q: What did Akash say when the boys asked about Kunal?
qa.a: "It's his business."

qa.q: What might Akash have felt when the boys teased Kunal?
qa.a: He probably felt protective and uncomfortable, torn between the group and his loyalty to Kunal.

qa.q: Why was Hansa's response to the teasing helpful?
qa.a: She thanked Akash privately and spoke to the teasers, supporting loyalty and stopping unkindness.

qa.q: How might Kunal see Akash after this?
qa.a: As a friend he can truly trust, someone who keeps his private things safe.

grounding: Shows a child's friendship growing from playmates to loyalty when he keeps a friend's confidence.

passage:
Sunday. Uday's diary.
Preeti told me something today she's never told anyone. She still sleeps with a torch because the dark scares her. She made me swear on my cricket bat. Last year we just played kho-kho together and that was it. Now she tells me things. At lunch Rinku was making fun of "babies who are scared of the dark," and looked at me like I knew something. My face got hot, but I didn't say anything. Later Preeti squeezed my arm and whispered, "Thanks." I think that's what a real friend is. I'm keeping the secret forever.

qa.q: What did Preeti make Uday swear on?
qa.a: Uday's cricket bat.

qa.q: How did Uday feel when Rinku looked over at lunch?
qa.a: Uday felt tense and uncomfortable, face hot, but determined to keep Preeti's secret.

qa.q: What does Uday's choice at lunch show about a good friend, and what could Uday do if the teasing continues?
qa.a: It shows loyalty; if the teasing continues, Uday could stand up for Preeti without revealing her secret, or tell a teacher about the teasing.

qa.q: How might Preeti feel about Uday after lunch?
qa.a: She likely feels grateful and safer, trusting Uday even more.

grounding: A child's diary shows a friendship deepening from simple play to keeping a shared secret loyally.

passage: Behind the temple pond in Raichur, Pankaj and Chandrika had a secret. Last summer they had only played gilli-danda with everyone else. This year they'd found a hollow in the old peepal tree and hid a tin there with their best marbles, a peacock feather and a map they'd drawn. Nobody else knew. One evening, Chandrika's older brother asked, "Where do you two disappear?" Pankaj looked at Chandrika, then at the pond. "Just walking." Later, alone, they checked the tin. Chandrika grinned at him. "You didn't tell." "Never," Pankaj said, and they touched thumbs.

qa.q: What did they keep in the tin?
qa.a: Their best marbles, a peacock feather and a map they'd drawn.

qa.q: What was Chandrika feeling when she said "You didn't tell"?
qa.a: She felt happy and reassured that she could trust Pankaj with their secret.

qa.q: How could Pankaj and Chandrika keep their secret without hurting others?
qa.a: They could keep the tin private but still play with the other children, so the friendship doesn't feel like shutting everyone out.

qa.q: How might Chandrika's brother see the two of them disappearing?
qa.a: He might feel curious or a little left out, wondering what they are doing.

grounding: Two village children move from group play to a close friendship with a shared hidden tin.

passage: At the public pool in Kraków, Tomas noticed his friend Ivan never went into the deep end. "Are you scared?" Tomas asked quietly while the others were racing. Ivan went red. "I can't really swim. Don't tell anyone." Tomas didn't. Instead, every Saturday for a month he met Ivan at the pool early, before their class came, and they practised floating by the wall. When their classmate Kasia asked why Tomas was always early, he said, "Just like the quiet." By May, Ivan swam a whole length. He climbed out and slapped Tomas's hand, grinning.

qa.q: When did Tomas meet Ivan at the pool?
qa.a: Every Saturday for a month, early, before their class came.

qa.q: How did Ivan feel when he admitted he couldn't really swim?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed, going red, and worried others would find out.

qa.q: What did Tomas do well as a friend?
qa.a: He kept Ivan's secret and helped him practise quietly instead of teasing him.

qa.q: How might Kasia see Tomas always being early?
qa.a: Kasia might find it a bit odd or curious, not knowing the real reason.

grounding: A boy keeps his friend's secret about not swimming and helps him practise quietly, deepening their friendship.

passage:
The hostel dorm at the boarding school was quiet after lights-out. Jasleen, eleven, whispered from the top bunk.

"Gargi, can I tell you something? You can't tell anyone."

"Promise."

"I still sleep with my old cloth rabbit. I hide it under my pillow."

Gargi was silent for a moment. "I have a blanket from my Nani. I smell it when I miss home."

Jasleen laughed softly. "Really?"

"Really. Our secret."

The next morning, when a girl teased Jasleen about her pillow, Gargi changed the subject quickly. Jasleen caught her eye and smiled.

qa.q: What does Jasleen hide under her pillow?
qa.a: She hides her old cloth rabbit.

qa.q: How did Jasleen feel when Gargi shared her own secret?
qa.a: Jasleen felt relieved and close to Gargi, laughing softly.

qa.q: How did Gargi show loyalty the next morning?
qa.a: She changed the subject when someone teased Jasleen, protecting her secret.

qa.q: How might Gargi feel sharing her Nani's blanket secret?
qa.a: Gargi likely felt a bit shy but trusting, glad to have a close friend.

grounding: In a boarding-school hostel, two children deepen their friendship by sharing and protecting each other's secrets.

passage:
I'm Thomas, Francis's older brother. This Christmas, I noticed Francis and his friend Alwin had changed.

Last year they just played football. Now they sat on the church steps for hours, talking quietly. Once I heard Alwin say, "Don't tell anyone, okay?" and Francis said, "Never."

Later, Alwin's cousin asked Francis what they'd been whispering about. Francis just said, "Football." Even I didn't find out.

I'm not sure what the secret was. But Francis seemed proud to be trusted with it.

qa.q: Where did Francis and Alwin sit for hours?
qa.a: They sat on the church steps.

qa.q: How might Francis have felt keeping Alwin's secret?
qa.a: Thomas thinks Francis seemed proud and loyal to be trusted with it.

qa.q: How can parents support friendships like this?
qa.a: They can respect the boys' privacy while making sure the friends know they can share any worrying secrets with an adult.

qa.q: How does Thomas see the change in Francis's friendship?
qa.a: Thomas notices it has grown deeper and more private since last year.

grounding: An older brother observes his brother's friendship growing deeper through shared secrets during Christmas.

passage:
Before Eid: Zainab and Vaibhav, both ten, cycle together every evening but talk only about games.

During Eid week: Vaibhav comes to Zainab's house for sheer khurma. He's quiet. On the roof, he says, "My Dadi moved to Mumbai. I miss her. Don't tell the others." Zainab says, "I won't," and tells him about her grandfather in Lucknow, whom she misses too.

Two weeks after Eid: A boy teases Vaibhav for being "moody". Zainab says, "Leave him," and doesn't explain. On the way home, Vaibhav says, "You didn't tell." She says, "Obviously."

qa.q: Where did Vaibhav's Dadi move?
qa.a: His Dadi moved to Mumbai.

qa.q: How did Vaibhav feel when he told Zainab about his Dadi?
qa.a: Vaibhav felt sad and lonely, missing his Dadi, and trusted Zainab with it.

qa.q: What showed that Zainab was a loyal friend?
qa.a: She kept his secret when he was teased and defended him without explaining.

qa.q: How might Zainab feel when Vaibhav said "You didn't tell"?
qa.a: Zainab likely felt proud and warm, as if keeping his trust was obvious.

grounding: Around Eid, two children move from playmates to loyal friends who share and keep secrets.

passage: Beta, you want to know about my oldest friend? I'm your Vandana Nani, and at ten I thought friends were just whoever sat beside me. Then, the monsoon I turned eleven, Gurleen moved into our lane. One wet afternoon under the neem tree, she told me she couldn't swim and was terrified of the school picnic at the river. She made me pinky-swear not to tell. At the picnic the other girls splashed and shouted, "Come in!" I said, "Gurleen's helping me collect shells," and we walked the bank together. She squeezed my hand. Sixty years later, she still calls me every monsoon.

qa.q: What did Gurleen tell Vandana under the neem tree?
qa.a: She told her she couldn't swim and was terrified of the school picnic at the river.

qa.q: What did young Vandana want when she said Gurleen was helping her collect shells?
qa.a: She wanted to spare Gurleen embarrassment, feeling loyal and protective of her friend's secret.

qa.q: Which choice at the picnic mattered most, and why?
qa.a: Keeping the promise and giving Gurleen a reason to stay on the bank protected her secret, and turned a new neighbour into a lifelong friend.

qa.q: What was the picnic like for Gurleen?
qa.a: Gurleen was scared of the water and the girls' shouting, so Vandana's help probably brought her huge relief.

grounding: Shows a child's friendship deepening into loyalty when she keeps a friend's secret, told as a grandmother's memory.
